entries.test: Public documentation of a system reaching AGI through only increased data and compute on existing LLM architectures would falsify the forecast; scaling-law research would establish their empirical status.
entries.note: Combines an undated forecast with a present methodological claim. Continued failure to reach AGI would not conclusively establish the forecast.

entries.test: Published model methods and comparative evaluations would show whether the advances discussed depended on techniques beyond pure scaling and whether test-time compute delivered partial improvements.
entries.note: The normalization broadens the claim to progress generally and turns a tentative qualification about current effectiveness into a definite limitation.
This is an endorsed recommendation about research methods.

entries.test: DeepSeek R1's published technical documentation would show whether its neural training incorporates explicit symbolic rules in its reward system.
entries.note: The surrounding text supplies R1 as the example and defines the intended sense of neurosymbolic.
There is no shared threshold for a system deserving the GPT-5 name or for counting huge advances. This is not merely a claim about whether a product named GPT-5 had launched.

entries.test: Public investment figures, contemporary scaling expectations, and cross-domain model evaluations from August 2022 through publication would show whether spending and pure-scaling gains matched the expectations described.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph anchors the expectations to continued broad capability leaps from more data and compute.

entries.test: Cross-domain evaluations of test-time compute systems available at publication, compared with earlier models and the GPT-3-to-GPT-4 transition, would show how broadly their improvements extended.
entries.note: Coding and math are examples, not an exhaustive list.

entries.test: Publicly reproducible outputs and evaluations of the systems available at publication would establish whether they exhibited hallucinations and reasoning errors.
entries.note: The normalization faithfully extracts the substantive performance claim.
“Apparently” qualifies the allegation rather than committing firmly to fabrication.

entries.test: Public scaling results, competing models' performance, competitive advantages, and pricing would show whether the stated plateau coincided with convergence, diminishing returns, and price competition.
entries.note: “Essentially no moat” becomes the stronger “no moat.” Marcus says immediately afterward that the predicted era has already arrived.

entries.test: Benchmark convergence, marginal scaling gains, evidence of durable competitive advantages, and public pricing through publication would establish whether the described market conditions existed.
entries.note: The antecedent describes “essentially no moat,” not an absolute absence of any moat.

entries.test: Contemporaneous benchmarks, dated pricing changes, and public reporting or company statements about competitive responses would establish DeepSeek's performance and its role in OpenAI's price reductions.
entries.note: Causal attribution requires more than showing that a price cut followed DeepSeek's release.

entries.test: Public comparisons of model capabilities, substitutability, switching costs, and pricing at publication would show whether suppliers largely competed as interchangeable offerings.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a plain economic meaning for commodity.

entries.test: The 2022 essay, subsequent cross-domain scaling results, evidence about the necessity of symbolic techniques, and documented model errors would establish whether the specified predictions were borne out by publication.
entries.note: The normalization removes the qualified retrospective framing and the express concession about Deep Research.
The normalization turns trying to impose beliefs into actually imposing them. The broader accusation supplies no shared test for imposing beliefs on science or solving its underlying challenges.
